item.title: Rain Rain Rain
item.description: We had some terrible rain the evening I arrived. Some places got 6-10 inches in 24 hours, and there’s still flooding in Lincoln. I drove 2.5 hours from the airport to Shelley’s house Wednesday night in some of the worst weather I’ve ever experienced. Couldn’t see the road at all on the interstate. Thank goodness I could tuck in behind slow semis and follow their hazard lights for miles. I honestly don’t know how I made it!

item.title: Starting Harvest
item.description: Keith says, “I thought I’d share that we started picking on your farm late yesterday afternoon. It seems like really good corn so far! It is also coming out really dry, I think one load I hauled in today was 14.8% moisture. I haven’t gotten to take many pictures of the harvest but I managed to get 2 last night so I will include them.  First picture is our very first pass though the field second picture I just thought the sunset looked neat with the combine.” (The photos are actually reversed below, because sunset!)

item.description: Keith is harvesting the soybeans today! He says, “They actually aren’t too bad considering what they have been through. They still might actually make 80bu an acre.”

item.title: Ride in the combine (video)
item.description: Loved my first ride in the combine, and learning about all the technology they use. These machines are so sophisticated! The heads push the crops toward a cutter, and then the cobs are conveyed to a threshing drum that beats them to break and shake the kernels away. The stalks and chaff are separated from the grain, which goes into a tank. When the tank is full, the driver can switch on an elevator to shoot it out of a pipe into a trailer that someone else (in this case, Keith) drives alongside the combine.

item.title: "Helping" harvest
item.description: With our farmer, Keith, “helping” harvest 25 acres.

item.title: Dad in the combine
item.description: Keith got done picking corn on the farm today. He says, “It was really good (244bu/ac) and really dry (15% moisture).  I’m glad we got it out when we did because it was starting to fall in today’s wind.  Your dad came out and rode along with dad. I think he really enjoyed it.  I took some pictures today including one of your dad in the combine. I was really sneaky so I don’t think he knows I I took it. "
